articulation.label: practice
articulation.alt: practice: /p/ → /r/ → /æ/ → /k/ → /t/ → /ɪ/ → /s/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /p/: Close the lips, then release the air.
/r/: Bunch the tongue; leave space at the ridge.
/æ/: Low front tongue; open the jaw.
/k/: Back of tongue meets the soft palate; release.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
/ɪ/: Front tongue, a little lower and relaxed.
/s/: Make a narrow gap near the ridge; let air flow.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Your A1 final check
sections: Try the five tasks before opening the models. A partner may speak slowly or repeat. Listen to the dictation and write what you hear.
Introduce yourself, spell a name and exchange basic personal details.
Order a meal and ask a new price chosen by your partner.
Ask the way to a place. Check one direction you hear.
Write a short message with a meeting day, place and time.

Congratulate your partner on finishing a course. Wish them success and agree to keep in touch.
Review words: again, now, restaurant, March, error. Cover the list; recall meanings and use two in your own sentences.
cards.name: Everyday English - A1 - Day 180 - Review & Check - 01

segments.name: Heart
segments.text: Use English a little every day.

cards.answer:
Dictation: Use English a little every day.
1: Give a name, place and one role. Ask your partner a relevant question.
2: Check the food, quantity and price. Ask for repetition if you do not hear it.
3: For example: Where is the library? Do I turn left here?
4: For example: Let’s meet at the library on Monday at ten. Please bring your book.
5: Sample answer: Congratulations on finishing the course. Good luck with your next class. Let us keep in touch.
For each task, note: I can do it; I can do it with repetition; I need more practice. Repeat difficult tasks another day with new details. Clear meaning matters more than a perfect accent.
